summary: Ephemeral GKE Workload Identity token issuance blocked by auth-syncer deny on service account bindings
description:
Issue summary:
Auth-syncer (the internal config-sync agent that enforces org-level IAM bindings and conditional denies) started applying a deny condition to service account impersonation bindings that unintentionally blocked GKE Workload Identity (WIF) token exchanges for ephemeral staging clusters.

Impact:
- New ephemeral GKE pod launches in staging that rely on WIF to exchange workload provider tokens for Google service account tokens fail to obtain tokens.
- Affecting ephemeral provisioning and debug workflows for multiple internal teams and CI jobs that use GPU-backed staging clusters.
- No customer-facing outage, but developer productivity is severely impacted and a Dedicated onboarding test pipeline failed.

Environment:
- staging-us-central1 (ephemeral GKE clusters created by the provisioning job)
- auth-syncer v1.4.0 (rolled out 2026-03-09 at 02:00 UTC)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Provision ephemeral GKE cluster via infra/provisioner in staging (job: infra/ephemeral-provision).
2. Deploy pod with Workload Identity annotation referencing provider: 'projects/XXX/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/redwood-pool/providers/infra'.
3. Inside pod, run: curl -sS --fail -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" "http://metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" or trigger the token-exchange path in k8s node identity agent.

Observed behavior:
- Token exchange fails with HTTP 403 and error snippet in control-plane logs: "PermissionDenied: Caller does not have permission to impersonate service account projects/XXX/serviceAccounts/ephemeral-staging-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
- Auth-syncer audit logs show a deny applied with condition: resource.matchLabels[env] != 'prod'.

Expected behavior:
- WIF token exchange succeeds for staging workloads; auth-syncer should not apply deny rules that prevent workload identity service account impersonation for ephemeral clusters.

Initial mitigation:
- Rolled back auth-syncer to v1.3.2 (pre-change) at 2026-03-12 19:40 UTC which removed the conditional deny and restored token issuance for subsequent ephemeral launches.
- Requeued failing pipelines and confirmed token issuance for newly created pods after rollback.

Next steps (high level):
- Root-cause analysis to determine why the new deny condition was applied and why WIF was not excluded by existing allowlist rules.
- Implement a test in the auth-syncer canary that simulates WIF token exchanges for non-prod clusters.
- Patch auth-syncer to add an explicit allowlist for workload-identity-pool serviceAccountTokenCreator bindings or to limit deny scope to human-managed service accounts only.
- Create a short-term org-policy exception for staging WIF pools if needed during rollout.

Owner: Marco Rivera (SRE)

2026-03-11 03:42 - SRE Oncall (A. Kim): Reproduced locally: token exchange fails with exact error 'PermissionDenied: Caller does not have permission to impersonate service account'. Auth-syncer audit: deny binding with condition 'resource.matchLabels[env] != "prod"'. Suspect rule was authored to protect production SAs but miscompiled. Blocking ephemeral provisioning.
2026-03-12 20:05 - Marco Rivera: Rolled back auth-syncer to v1.3.2 across staging. Confirmed new ephemeral pods can exchange tokens. Rolling update paused until patch is ready.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Security (L. Nguyen): Noted that the deny was intended to prevent cross-project human account impersonation; we'll review policy authoring guidelines to avoid excluding service account flows. Recommending explicit tests in PR gating.

2026-03-14 11:15 - Priya Shah: CI owners asked for a short-term exception to the deny for the redwood-pool WIF provider while patch lands. Filing request with infra-ops for org-policy temporary exception.
